# Load Libraries
```{julia}
#| output: false
using Pumas
using Random
using Distributions
using LinearAlgebra
using Statistics
using DataFrames
using Bioequivalence
using CairoMakie
using Makie
using Logging
```

# Set Random Seed
```{julia}
#| output: false
Random.seed!(142)
```

# PK Model

Same model as the parallel-design version. `tvbio` controls relative bioavailability
of Test vs Reference via `@dosecontrol`, so AUC_T/AUC_R = tvbio exactly.

```{julia}
#| output: false
pkmodel = @model begin
    @param begin
        tvcl  ∈ RealDomain(lower=0)
        tvv   ∈ RealDomain(lower=0)
        tvka  ∈ RealDomain(lower=0)
        tvbio ∈ RealDomain(lower=0)
        Ω     ∈ PDiagDomain(3)
        σ     ∈ RealDomain(lower=0)
    end

    @random begin
        η ~ MvNormal(Ω)
    end

    @covariates TRT

    @pre begin
        CL  = tvcl * exp(η[1])
        V   = tvv  * exp(η[2])
        Ka  = tvka * exp(η[3])
    end

    @dosecontrol begin
        bioav = (Depot = TRT == "T" ? tvbio : 1.0,)
    end

    @dynamics begin
        Depot'   = -Ka * Depot
        Central' =  Ka * Depot - (CL / V) * Central
    end

    @derived begin
        cp = @. Central / V
        dv ~ @. Normal(cp, σ)
    end
end
```

# True Parameter Values
```{julia}
#| output: false
θ_true = (
    tvcl  = 5.0,
    tvv   = 50.0,
    tvka  = 1.2,
    tvbio = 1.0,
    Ω     = Diagonal([0.09, 0.09, 0.09]),   # ~30% CV IIV
    σ     = 0.2
)
```

# Crossover Simulation Helpers

## Design rationale

In a **2x2 crossover design**, each subject receives both Test (T) and Reference (R)
formulations in separate periods with an adequate washout between them. The same
between-subject random effects (eta) apply to both periods for a given subject.

**Key difference from parallel design:** The within-subject comparison eliminates
between-subject variability from the BE assessment, resulting in narrower confidence
intervals and higher statistical power for the same number of total observations.

The simulation ensures the same eta is used for both T and R periods by:

1. Sampling eta once per subject from `MvNormal(0, Omega)`
2. Incorporating eta into subject-specific typical values
3. Simulating both R and T periods with these fixed individual parameters
   and a near-zero residual IIV (so only residual error sigma differs between periods)

```{julia}
#| output: false
"""Create parallel-design population (used only for parameter estimation)."""
function create_be_population(n_per_arm)
    subjects = Subject[]
    for trt in ["R", "T"], i in 1:n_per_arm
        push!(subjects, Subject(
            id     = length(subjects) + 1,
            events = DosageRegimen(100, time = 0),
            covariates = (TRT = trt,)
        ))
    end
    return Population(subjects)
end

"""Simulate a parallel BE trial (used only for parameter estimation)."""
function simulate_be_trial(params; n_per_arm = 30)
    pop = create_be_population(n_per_arm)
    return simobs(pkmodel, pop, params; obstimes = 0:1:72)
end

"""
Simulate a 2x2 crossover BE trial.

Each of `n_subjects` subjects receives both R and T with the **same individual eta**.
Returns a NamedTuple with :R (vector of R-period sims), :T (vector of T-period sims),
and :n_subjects.
"""
function simulate_crossover_trial(params; n_subjects = 30)
    # Sample between-subject random effects once per subject
    ηs = [rand(MvNormal(zeros(3), params.Ω)) for _ in 1:n_subjects]
    tiny_Ω = Diagonal(fill(1e-8, 3))   # near-zero — IIV already baked into typical values

    sims_R = Vector{Any}(undef, n_subjects)
    sims_T = Vector{Any}(undef, n_subjects)

    for i in 1:n_subjects
        η = ηs[i]
        # Individual parameters: absorb η into typical values
        ind_p = (
            tvcl  = params.tvcl * exp(η[1]),
            tvv   = params.tvv  * exp(η[2]),
            tvka  = params.tvka * exp(η[3]),
            tvbio = params.tvbio,
            Ω     = tiny_Ω,
            σ     = params.σ
        )

        subj_R = Subject(id = i,              events = DosageRegimen(100, time = 0), covariates = (TRT = "R",))
        subj_T = Subject(id = i + n_subjects, events = DosageRegimen(100, time = 0), covariates = (TRT = "T",))

        sims_R[i] = simobs(pkmodel, subj_R, ind_p; obstimes = 0:1:72)
        sims_T[i] = simobs(pkmodel, subj_T, ind_p; obstimes = 0:1:72)
    end

    return (R = sims_R, T = sims_T, n_subjects = n_subjects)
end
```

# Simulate Reference Trial and Fit

Parameter estimation uses a parallel-design trial (identical to v2) to obtain
model parameter estimates and their uncertainty. The study design for virtual BE
trials (crossover here) is independent of the design used for estimation.

```{julia}
#| output: false
ref_sim = simulate_be_trial(θ_true; n_per_arm = 30)

sim_pop = read_pumas(
    DataFrame(ref_sim);
    id = :id, time = :time, observations = [:dv],
    amt = :amt, evid = :evid, covariates = [:TRT], cmt = :cmt
)

init = (
    tvcl  = 4.5,
    tvv   = 45.0,
    tvka  = 1.0,
    tvbio = 1.0,
    Ω     = Diagonal([0.1, 0.1, 0.1]),
    σ     = 0.3
)

fit_res = fit(pkmodel, sim_pop, init, Pumas.FOCE())
θ̂ = coef(fit_res)
nothing
```

# Uncertainty Extraction

## Sampling helper
```{julia}
#| output: false
"""
Sample `n` parameter NamedTuples from a MvNormal on the estimation (log) scale.
`mean_params` is a NamedTuple of point estimates (original scale).
`V` is the variance-covariance matrix on the estimation scale.
"""
function sample_from_vcov(mean_params, V, n)
    μ = [
        log(mean_params.tvcl), log(mean_params.tvv),
        log(mean_params.tvka), log(mean_params.tvbio),
        log(mean_params.Ω[1,1]), log(mean_params.Ω[2,2]), log(mean_params.Ω[3,3]),
        log(mean_params.σ)
    ]
    dist = MvNormal(μ, Symmetric(V))
    return [begin
        s = rand(dist)
        (tvcl  = exp(s[1]), tvv  = exp(s[2]),
         tvka  = exp(s[3]), tvbio = exp(s[4]),
         Ω     = Diagonal([exp(s[5]), exp(s[6]), exp(s[7])]),
         σ     = exp(s[8]))
    end for _ in 1:n]
end
```

## Method 1: VCOV (Asymptotic Normal)
```{julia}
#| output: false
vcov_param_samples = sample_from_vcov(θ̂, vcov(fit_res), 200)
```

## Method 2: Bootstrap
```{julia}
#| output: false
boot_settings = Bootstrap(
    samples = 100,
    stratify_by = nothing,
    ensemblealg = EnsembleThreads()
)
boot_inf = infer(fit_res, boot_settings; level = 0.95)

boot_param_samples = sample_from_vcov(coef(boot_inf), vcov(boot_inf), 200)
nothing
```

## Method 3: SIR
```{julia}
#| output: false
sir_settings = SIR(samples = 200, resamples = 100)
sir_inf = infer(fit_res, sir_settings; level = 0.95)

sir_param_samples = sample_from_vcov(coef(sir_inf), vcov(sir_inf), 200)
nothing
```

# TOST for Crossover-Design BE

## Paired TOST and NCA helpers

In a crossover design the TOST uses **within-subject (paired) differences** on the
log scale. Compared with the parallel-design (unpaired) TOST:

| Component | Parallel | Crossover |
|---|---|---|
| Difference | mean(log T) - mean(log R) | mean(d_i), d_i = log T_i - log R_i |
| SE | sqrt(sp^2 (1/n_R + 1/n_T)) | sd(d) / sqrt(n) |
| df | n_R + n_T - 2 | n - 1 |
| Variability driver | Total (BSV + WSV) | Within-subject only |

Because between-subject variability cancels in the within-subject difference,
crossover CIs are typically much narrower, yielding higher power.

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| echo: false
"""
Two One-Sided Tests for a 2x2 crossover design.
Uses within-subject (paired) differences on the log scale.
Returns GMR, 90% CI bou nds, and pass/fail status.
"""
function tost_test_crossover(log_R, log_T; alpha = 0.05, θ_L = 0.80, θ_U = 1.25)
    n = length(log_R)
    n < 2 && return (gmr=NaN, ci_lo=NaN, ci_hi=NaN, pass=false)

    d  = log_T .- log_R           # within-subject log-differences
    Δ  = mean(d)
    se = std(d) / sqrt(n)
    df = n - 1
    tc = quantile(TDist(df), 1 - alpha)

    gmr   = exp(Δ)
    ci_lo = exp(Δ - tc * se)
    ci_hi = exp(Δ + tc * se)
    pass  = ci_lo >= θ_L && ci_hi <= θ_U

    return (gmr=gmr, ci_lo=ci_lo, ci_hi=ci_hi, pass=pass)
end

"""Find first matching column from `candidates` in DataFrame `df`."""
function find_col(df, candidates)
    ns = names(df)
    for c in candidates
        if string(c) in ns
            return Symbol(c)
        end
    end
    error("None of $candidates found in columns: $ns")
end

# Detect AUC and Cmax column names once from the reference NCA table
const AUC_COL  = find_col(nca_tbl_ref, ["aucinf_obs", "aucinf", "auclast", "AUC", "auc"])
const CMAX_COL = find_col(nca_tbl_ref, ["cmax", "Cmax", "CMAX"])
println("Using NCA columns: AUC = $AUC_COL, Cmax = $CMAX_COL")

"""Convert a vector of individual simobs results to a sorted NCA report table."""
function sims_to_nca(sims)
    simdf = vcat([DataFrame(s) for s in sims]...)
    simdf.route .= "ev"
    simdf.dv .= max.(simdf.dv, 0.0)

    tbl = with_logger(NullLogger()) do
        ncapop = read_nca(simdf;
            id = :id, time = :time, amt = :amt,
            observations = :dv, route = :route
        )
        nca_out = run_nca(ncapop)
        nca_out.reportdf
    end
    return sort(tbl, :id)
end

"""Extract non-missing, positive values from a column as Float64 vector."""
function clean_pk_col(df, col)
    vals = df[!, col]
    return Float64[v for v in vals if !ismissing(v) && v > 0]
end

"""
Run NCA on a crossover trial, then apply paired TOST to AUC and Cmax.
Returns detailed results: GMR, 90% CI bounds, and pass/fail for each metric.
Returns `nothing` if insufficient paired data.
"""
function run_be_on_crossover_detailed(trial)
    tbl_R = sims_to_nca(trial.R)
    tbl_T = sims_to_nca(trial.T)

    n_pairs = min(nrow(tbl_R), nrow(tbl_T))
    n_pairs < 2 && return nothing

    # Build paired log-vectors — drop pairs where either value is missing/non-positive
    auc_lR,  auc_lT  = Float64[], Float64[]
    cmax_lR, cmax_lT = Float64[], Float64[]

    for i in 1:n_pairs
        ar, at = tbl_R[i, AUC_COL],  tbl_T[i, AUC_COL]
        cr, ct = tbl_R[i, CMAX_COL], tbl_T[i, CMAX_COL]

        if !ismissing(ar) && !ismissing(at) && ar > 0 && at > 0
            push!(auc_lR, log(Float64(ar)))
            push!(auc_lT, log(Float64(at)))
        end
        if !ismissing(cr) && !ismissing(ct) && cr > 0 && ct > 0
            push!(cmax_lR, log(Float64(cr)))
            push!(cmax_lT, log(Float64(ct)))
        end
    end

    (length(auc_lR) < 2 || length(cmax_lR) < 2) && return nothing

    auc_res  = tost_test_crossover(auc_lR,  auc_lT)
    cmax_res = tost_test_crossover(cmax_lR, cmax_lT)

    return (
        auc_gmr=auc_res.gmr, auc_lo=auc_res.ci_lo, auc_hi=auc_res.ci_hi, auc_pass=auc_res.pass,
        cmax_gmr=cmax_res.gmr, cmax_lo=cmax_res.ci_lo, cmax_hi=cmax_res.ci_hi, cmax_pass=cmax_res.pass,
        overall_pass=auc_res.pass && cmax_res.pass
    )
end
```

# Within-Subject %CV Estimation Helper
```{julia}
#| output: false
#| echo: false
"""
Estimate within-subject (intra-subject) %CV for AUC and Cmax from simulated
crossover trials at T/R = 1.0.

In a 2x2 crossover: var(d_i) = 2 * sigma^2_ws, so sigma^2_ws = var(d) / 2.
%CV_ws = 100 * sqrt(exp(sigma^2_ws) - 1).
"""
function estimate_cv_crossover(param_samples; n_subjects = 60, n_reps = 50)
    auc_ws_vars  = Float64[]
    cmax_ws_vars = Float64[]

    for _ in 1:n_reps
        θ_draw     = param_samples[rand(1:length(param_samples))]
        sim_params = merge(θ_draw, (tvbio = 1.0,))

        try
            trial = simulate_crossover_trial(sim_params; n_subjects = n_subjects)
            tbl_R = sims_to_nca(trial.R)
            tbl_T = sims_to_nca(trial.T)

            n_pairs = min(nrow(tbl_R), nrow(tbl_T))

            auc_d  = Float64[]
            cmax_d = Float64[]

            for i in 1:n_pairs
                ar, at = tbl_R[i, AUC_COL],  tbl_T[i, AUC_COL]
                cr, ct = tbl_R[i, CMAX_COL], tbl_T[i, CMAX_COL]

                if !ismissing(ar) && !ismissing(at) && ar > 0 && at > 0
                    push!(auc_d, log(Float64(at)) - log(Float64(ar)))
                end
                if !ismissing(cr) && !ismissing(ct) && cr > 0 && ct > 0
                    push!(cmax_d, log(Float64(ct)) - log(Float64(cr)))
                end
            end

            # Within-subject variance = var(d) / 2
            length(auc_d)  >= 2 && push!(auc_ws_vars,  var(auc_d)  / 2)
            length(cmax_d) >= 2 && push!(cmax_ws_vars, var(cmax_d) / 2)
        catch
            continue
        end
    end

    auc_cv  = 100 * sqrt(exp(mean(auc_ws_vars))  - 1)
    cmax_cv = 100 * sqrt(exp(mean(cmax_ws_vars)) - 1)
    return (auc_cv=auc_cv, cmax_cv=cmax_cv)
end
```

# Virtual BE Simulation Engine (Crossover)
```{julia}
#| output: false
#| code-summary: "Virtual BE simulation engine — crossover design (click to expand)"
const SAMPLE_SIZES = [12, 24, 30, 40, 50, 60, 80]
const TR_RATIOS    = [0.7, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.3]

"""
Run virtual crossover BE simulations across all combinations of T/R ratios and
sample sizes.

**n_subjects** = total subjects per trial. Each subject receives both T and R
(contrast with parallel design where n_per_arm subjects receive only one treatment).

Returns a NamedTuple with :summary (aggregated pass rates) and :detailed (per-sim GMR/CI).
"""
function virtual_be_sim(param_samples, method_name;
                        tr_ratios       = TR_RATIOS,
                        n_subjects_list = SAMPLE_SIZES,
                        n_sims          = 200)

    summary_results = DataFrame(
        method     = String[],
        tr_ratio   = Float64[],
        n_subjects = Int[],
        n_pass     = Int[],
        n_valid    = Int[],
        n_error    = Int[],
        pass_rate  = Float64[]
    )

    detailed_results = DataFrame(
        method       = String[],
        tr_ratio     = Float64[],
        n_subjects   = Int[],
        sim_id       = Int[],
        auc_gmr      = Float64[],
        auc_lo       = Float64[],
        auc_hi       = Float64[],
        auc_pass     = Bool[],
        cmax_gmr     = Float64[],
        cmax_lo      = Float64[],
        cmax_hi      = Float64[],
        cmax_pass    = Bool[],
        overall_pass = Bool[]
    )

    total_combos = length(n_subjects_list) * length(tr_ratios)
    combo = 0

    for n_subj in n_subjects_list, tr in tr_ratios
        combo += 1
        n_pass  = 0
        n_error = 0

        for i in 1:n_sims
            θ_draw     = param_samples[rand(1:length(param_samples))]
            sim_params = merge(θ_draw, (tvbio = tr,))

            try
                trial = simulate_crossover_trial(sim_params; n_subjects = n_subj)
                res   = run_be_on_crossover_detailed(trial)

                if res === nothing
                    n_error += 1
                else
                    res.overall_pass && (n_pass += 1)
                    push!(detailed_results, (
                        method       = method_name,
                        tr_ratio     = tr,
                        n_subjects   = n_subj,
                        sim_id       = i,
                        auc_gmr      = res.auc_gmr,
                        auc_lo       = res.auc_lo,
                        auc_hi       = res.auc_hi,
                        auc_pass     = res.auc_pass,
                        cmax_gmr     = res.cmax_gmr,
                        cmax_lo      = res.cmax_lo,
                        cmax_hi      = res.cmax_hi,
                        cmax_pass    = res.cmax_pass,
                        overall_pass = res.overall_pass
                    ))
                end
            catch e
                n_error += 1
                # silently count errors
            end
        end

        n_valid = n_sims - n_error
        rate    = n_valid > 0 ? (n_pass / n_valid) * 100 : NaN

        push!(summary_results, (
            method     = method_name,
            tr_ratio   = tr,
            n_subjects = n_subj,
            n_pass     = n_pass,
            n_valid    = n_valid,
            n_error    = n_error,
            pass_rate  = rate
        ))

        # progress logged silently
    end

    return (summary = summary_results, detailed = detailed_results)
end
```

# Within-Subject %CV for Olanzapine (Crossover)

Within-subject (intra-subject) variability pooled from 100 simulated 2×2 crossover trials (60 subjects, T/R = 1.0). In crossover designs, this within-subject %CV — not total between-subject variability — drives CI width and power.

```{julia}
#| output: false
cv_estimates = estimate_cv_crossover(fixed_param_samples; n_subjects = 60, n_reps = 100)
nothing
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
println("AUC  within-subject %CV = $(round(cv_estimates.auc_cv, digits=1))%")
println("Cmax within-subject %CV = $(round(cv_estimates.cmax_cv, digits=1))%")
```

# Visualization: Pass Rate by T/R Ratio and Sample Size
```{julia}
#| label: fig-passrate-lines
#| fig-cap: "Crossover BE pass rate across T/R ratios and sample sizes for each uncertainty method."
fig1 = Figure(size = (1400, 900))
methods_list = ["Fixed", "VCOV", "Bootstrap", "SIR"]
size_colors  = [:indigo, :dodgerblue, :steelblue, :seagreen, :orange, :crimson, :darkred]

for (idx, m) in enumerate(methods_list)
    row = (idx - 1) ÷ 2 + 1
    col = (idx - 1) % 2 + 1
    ax = Axis(fig1[row, col];
        xlabel = "T/R Ratio",
        ylabel = "BE Pass Rate (%)",
        title  = "$m Method (Crossover)",
        xticks = TR_RATIOS,
        yticks = 0:10:100
    )

    sub = filter(r -> r.method == m, all_summary)
    for (j, n) in enumerate(SAMPLE_SIZES)
        sub_n = sort(filter(r -> r.n_subjects == n, sub), :tr_ratio)
        scatterlines!(ax, sub_n.tr_ratio, sub_n.pass_rate;
            label     = "n=$n",
            color     = size_colors[j],
            marker    = :circle,
            markersize = 8,
            linewidth = 2
        )
    end

    hlines!(ax, [5.0]; color = :red, linestyle = :dash, linewidth = 1, label = "5% α")
    vlines!(ax, [0.80, 1.25]; color = :gray70, linestyle = :dot, linewidth = 1)

    if idx == 2
        axislegend(ax; position = :rt, labelsize = 9)
    end
end

supertitle = Label(fig1[0, :], "Crossover BE Pass Rate by T/R Ratio and Sample Size"; fontsize = 20)
```

# Visualization: Pass Rate Heatmaps
```{julia}
#| label: fig-heatmaps
#| fig-cap: "Heatmap of crossover BE pass rates by sample size and T/R ratio."
fig2 = Figure(size = (1400, 900))

for (idx, m) in enumerate(methods_list)

    col = (idx - 1) % 2 + 1

    sub = filter(r -> r.method == m, all_summary)
    mat = zeros(length(SAMPLE_SIZES), length(TR_RATIOS))
    for (i, n) in enumerate(SAMPLE_SIZES), (j, tr) in enumerate(TR_RATIOS)
        r = filter(r -> r.n_subjects == n && r.tr_ratio == tr, sub)
        mat[i, j] = nrow(r) > 0 ? r.pass_rate[1] : NaN
    end

    ax = Axis(fig2[row, col];
        xlabel = "T/R Ratio",
        ylabel = "Subjects (Crossover)",
        title  = "$m Method (Crossover)",
        xticks = (1:length(TR_RATIOS), string.(TR_RATIOS)),
        yticks = (1:length(SAMPLE_SIZES), string.(SAMPLE_SIZES))
    )

    hm = heatmap!(ax, 1:length(TR_RATIOS), 1:length(SAMPLE_SIZES), mat';
        colormap = :RdYlGn, colorrange = (0, 100)
    )

    for (i, n) in enumerate(SAMPLE_SIZES), (j, tr) in enumerate(TR_RATIOS)
        txt = isnan(mat[i, j]) ? "—" : "$(round(Int, mat[i, j]))%"
        text!(ax, j, i; text = txt, align = (:center, :center),
            fontsize = 11, color = mat[i, j] > 50 ? :black : :white)
    end

    if idx == 2
        Colorbar(fig2[row, col + 1], hm; label = "Pass Rate (%)")
    end
end

supertitle2 = Label(fig2[0, :], "Crossover BE Pass Rate Heatmap: Sample Size vs T/R Ratio"; fontsize = 20)
fig2
```

```{julia}

    ax = Axis(fig4[1, j];
        xlabel = "AUC GMR",
        ylabel = j == 1 ? "Count" : "",

end
```

# Visualization: 90% CI Bounds (LB and UB) for AUC
```{julia}
#| label: fig-ci-bounds
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of AUC 90% CI lower and upper bounds (Fixed, n=30, Crossover)."
fig6 = Figure(size = (1400, 800))

for (j, tr) in enumerate(TR_RATIOS)
    sub_tr = filter(r -> r.tr_ratio == tr, detail_sub)
    nrow(sub_tr) == 0 && continue

    # Lower Bound
    ax_lb = Axis(fig6[1, j];
        xlabel = j == 3 ? "AUC 90% CI Lower Bound" : "",
        ylabel = j == 1 ? "Count" : "",
        title  = "T/R = $tr"
    )
    hist!(ax_lb, sub_tr.auc_lo; bins = 25, color = (:coral, 0.7), strokecolor = :black, strokewidth = 0.5)
    vlines!(ax_lb, [0.80]; color = :red, linestyle = :dash, linewidth = 2, label = "BE limit")

    # Upper Bound
    ax_ub = Axis(fig6[2, j];
        xlabel = j == 3 ? "AUC 90% CI Upper Bound" : "",
        ylabel = j == 1 ? "Count" : ""
    )
    hist!(ax_ub, sub_tr.auc_hi; bins = 25, color = (:mediumpurple, 0.7), strokecolor = :black, strokewidth = 0.5)
    vlines!(ax_ub, [1.25]; color = :red, linestyle = :dash, linewidth = 2, label = "BE limit")
end

Label(fig6[0, :], "AUC 90% CI Bounds Distribution (Fixed, n=30, Crossover)"; fontsize = 18)
Label(fig6[1, 0], "Lower Bound"; fontsize = 14, rotation = pi/2)
Label(fig6[2, 0], "Upper Bound"; fontsize = 14, rotation = pi/2)
fig6
```

# Visualization: Effect of Sample Size on CI Width
```{julia}
#| label: fig-ci-width
#| fig-cap: "Median AUC GMR and 90% CI bounds narrowing with increasing sample size (Crossover)."
fig7 = Figure(size = (1000, 600))

# Calculate median CI width (AUC) by sample size at T/R = 1.0
detail_tr1 = filter(r -> r.method == "Fixed" && r.tr_ratio == 1.0, all_detailed)

ci_width_summary = combine(
    groupby(detail_tr1, :n_subjects),
    :auc_lo  => median => :median_lb,
    :auc_hi  => median => :median_ub,
    :auc_gmr => median => :median_gmr,
    [:auc_hi, :auc_lo] => ((hi, lo) -> median(hi .- lo)) => :median_ci_width
)
sort!(ci_width_summary, :n_subjects)

ax7 = Axis(fig7[1, 1];
    xlabel = "Subjects (Crossover)",
    ylabel = "Value",
    title  = "AUC: Median GMR and 90% CI Bounds vs Sample Size (T/R = 1.0, Fixed, Crossover)",
    xticks = SAMPLE_SIZES
)

band!(ax7, ci_width_summary.n_subjects,
    ci_width_summary.median_lb, ci_width_summary.median_ub;
    color = (:steelblue, 0.3), label = "Median 90% CI")
scatterlines!(ax7, ci_width_summary.n_subjects, ci_width_summary.median_gmr;
    color = :steelblue, marker = :circle, markersize = 10, linewidth = 2, label = "Median GMR")
scatterlines!(ax7, ci_width_summary.n_subjects, ci_width_summary.median_lb;
    color = :coral, marker = :dtriangle, markersize = 8, linewidth = 1.5, linestyle = :dash, label = "Median LB")
scatterlines!(ax7, ci_width_summary.n_subjects, ci_width_summary.median_ub;
    color = :mediumpurple, marker = :utriangle, markersize = 8, linewidth = 1.5, linestyle = :dash, label = "Median UB")
hlines!(ax7, [0.80, 1.25]; color = :red, linestyle = :dot, linewidth = 1, label = "BE limits")

axislegend(ax7; position = :rt, labelsize = 10)
fig7
```
